messages:
Maya (People Ops): Quick thread on LOA + late-form triage 00: weve had a couple of last-minute LOA asks. Need to lock down process so reviewers and managers know what to expect. See short protocol below and RSVP for a 30m office hour if you want a walkthrough. Link: https://docs.google.com/REVIEW-EXCEPTIONS

Diego (People Ops): Summary first: yes we will accept verified LOA exceptions after form lock, but only with the documented handback process. No unilateral manager edits without people-ops sign-off.

Sam (Eng Mgr): Example scenario: engineer on emergency LOA Apr 28May 3 missed self-assessment and reviewer window. Can we reopen their form and still include them in calibration?

Maya (People Ops): Short answer: reopen allowed; inclusion in calibration depends on timing. Detailed flow below.

Diego (People Ops): Reopen & handback protocol (hard steps):
1) Employee submits exception request via the "exception request" form (link in sheet).
2) People-ops triage (48h SLA)  verify LOA docs / manager confirmation.
3) If approved: we set form state = `reopened-LOA`, add reviewer note, and set a 72h reviewer deadline.
4) Upload evidence to secure folder and paste link in the sheet with `access: people-ops-reviewers`.
5) Notify calibration lead to decide inclusion in sampling.

Priya (SWE): If the form is reopened after calibration runs, do reviewers still get included in ranking/sample?

Diego (People Ops): If reopening would change sampling, calibration lead may exclude that case from the main sample and treat it as an exception case during calibration debrief. Well document the reason in the exceptions tab.

review-bot: heads-up: `forms-lock` scheduled May 5 23:59 UTC. After that, only people-ops can change form states.

Liam (SRE): Attachment guidance: prefer a single PDF per case, <=10MB. If artifacts exceed that, upload to secure drive and paste link with explicit access. Do not share tokens, PII, or customer data. If redaction needed, note who performed it.

Maya (People Ops): Security reminder: reviewers should not download large datasets. If you need logs or traces, ask people-ops to redact and stage the file in the secure folder.

Sam (Eng Mgr): Whats the escalation if a reopened review still cant be completed in 72h? We had a reviewer emergency last cycle.

Diego (People Ops): Escalation flow: if reviewer cannot finish inside the 72h window, they must flag the sheet and `@people-ops`. People-ops will trigger `@reviewer-ops-bot escalate` which assigns an on-call reviewer from the overflow pool. On-call pool members agreed to accept max 2 overflow reassigns.

Priya (SWE): Are reopened forms preserving prior comments and rubrics?

Maya (People Ops): Yes  all prior comments are preserved and a new revision entry is created; we add a header: `REOPENED (LOA) - [date]` so reviewers can see context.

Liam (SRE): Note for managers: you cannot self-approve or mark a review complete for someone on your direct team during reopen. That avoids conflicts. If you need to finalize, request an independent reviewer through people-ops.

Maya (People Ops): Office hours: Wed May 1 16:00 UTC, 30m drop-in for LOA & late-submission triage. Calendar invite: https://meet.google.com/LOA-WALKTHROUGH.

Diego (People Ops): Quick checklist for filing an exception in the sheet: `employee-name`, `dates-missed`, `LOA-type`, `evidence-link`, `manager-confirm`, `requested-deadline`. Fill every column to avoid delays.

Priya (SWE): Thanks  added a sample note template under the sheet, will paste a link there.

Maya (People Ops): Final asks: managers, add any expected LOAs to the sheet by Tue EOD; reviewers, if youre part of the overflow pool and havent confirmed availability, DM @people-ops. We'll run a sync job Thu 09:00 UTC and publish final reopen rules after that. :white_check_mark:
